blocks.text: Alur Kerja Saat Query Lambat

items: Pastikan masalahnya nyata: ukur waktunya, jangan mengandalkan kesan "terasa lambat".
Jalankan EXPLAIN ANALYZE dan cari operasi yang membaca jauh lebih banyak baris daripada yang akhirnya dikembalikan.
Periksa apakah ada kebiasaan pematikan index dari Bab 18.5 pada query tersebut.
Periksa apakah index yang dibutuhkan memang ada, dan urutan kolomnya sesuai pola query.
Periksa statistik: bila estimasi baris meleset jauh dari aktual, jalankan ANALYZE atau UPDATE STATISTICS.
Pertimbangkan menulis ulang: subquery terkorelasi menjadi JOIN atau window function, atau memecah query raksasa dengan CTE.
Terapkan SATU perubahan, ukur ulang, lalu bandingkan. Beberapa perubahan sekaligus membuat Anda tidak tahu mana yang berhasil.

blocks.text: Penutup

Anda kini memiliki peta lengkap SQL relasional: dari membuat tabel dan mengisi data, mengambilnya dengan SELECT dan JOIN, meringkasnya dengan agregasi dan window function, sampai merancang skema yang sehat serta menjaganya tetap cepat dan aman.

Tiga hal yang paling menentukan penguasaan SQL. Pertama, pahami urutan eksekusi logis (Bab 6.3) — hampir semua kebingungan pemula bisa dijelaskan dari sana. Kedua, hormati NULL sebagai "tidak diketahui", bukan sebagai kosong atau nol. Ketiga, biasakan membaca EXPLAIN sejak dini, karena menulis query yang benar dan menulis query yang cepat adalah dua keterampilan yang berbeda.

Cara tercepat menjadi mahir bukan membaca lebih banyak, melainkan menjawab pertanyaan nyata dengan data nyata. Ambil data apa pun yang Anda miliki, ajukan pertanyaan yang benar-benar ingin Anda ketahui jawabannya, lalu susun query-nya. Selamat berlatih!

modules.title: SQL Notes: Jenis Perintah SQL (DDL, DML, DCL, TCL, DQL)
modules.summary: There are five types of SQL commands: DDL, DML, DCL, TCL, and DQL.

items: SQL commands are instructions. It is used to communicate with the database. It is also used to perform specific tasks, functions, and queries of data.
SQL can perform various tasks like create a table, add data to tables, drop the table, modify the table, set permission for users.

blocks.text: Types of SQL Commands
There are five types of SQL commands: DDL, DML, DCL, TCL, and DQL.
Data Definition Language (DDL)

items: DDL changes the structure of the table like creating a table, deleting a table, altering a table, etc.
All the command of DDL are auto-committed that means it permanently save all the changes in the database.

blocks.text: Here are some commands that come under DDL:

items: CREATE
ALTER
DROP
TRUNCATE

blocks.text: **a. CREATE** It is used to create a new table in the database.
**Syntax:**

blocks.code: CREATE TABLE TABLE_NAME (COLUMN_NAME DATATYPES[,....]);

blocks.text: **Example:**

blocks.code: CREATE TABLE EMPLOYEE(Name VARCHAR2(20), Email VARCHAR2(100), DOB DATE);

blocks.text: **b. DROP:** It is used to delete both the structure and record stored in the table.
**Syntax**

blocks.code: DROP TABLE ;

blocks.text: **Example**

blocks.code: DROP TABLE EMPLOYEE;

blocks.text: **c. ALTER:** It is used to alter the structure of the database. This change could be either to modify the characteristics of an existing attribute or probably to add a new attribute.
**Syntax:**
To add a new column in the table

blocks.code: ALTER TABLE table_name ADD column_name COLUMN-definition;

blocks.text: To modify existing column in the table:

blocks.code: ALTER TABLE MODIFY(COLUMN DEFINITION....);

blocks.text: **EXAMPLE**

blocks.code:
ALTER TABLE STU_DETAILS ADD(ADDRESS VARCHAR2(20));
ALTER TABLE STU_DETAILS MODIFY (NAME VARCHAR2(20));

blocks.text: **d. TRUNCATE:** It is used to delete all the rows from the table and free the space containing the table.
**Syntax:**

blocks.code: TRUNCATE TABLE table_name;

blocks.text: **Example:**

blocks.code: TRUNCATE TABLE EMPLOYEE;

blocks.text: Data Manipulation Language

items: DML commands are used to modify the database. It is responsible for all form of changes in the database.
The command of DML is not auto-committed that means it can't permanently save all the changes in the database. They can be rollback.

blocks.text: Here are some commands that come under DML:

items: INSERT
UPDATE
DELETE

blocks.text: **a. INSERT:** The INSERT statement is a SQL query. It is used to insert data into the row of a table.
**Syntax:**
Or

blocks.code:
INSERT INTO TABLE_NAME
VALUES (value1, value2, value3, .... valueN);

blocks.text: **For example:**

blocks.code: INSERT INTO javatpoint (Author, Subject) VALUES ("Sonoo", "DBMS");

blocks.text: **b. UPDATE:** This command is used to update or modify the value of a column in the table.
**Syntax:**

blocks.code: UPDATE table_name SET [column_name1= value1,...column_nameN = valueN] [WHERE CONDITION]

blocks.text: **For example:**

blocks.code:
UPDATE students
SET User_Name = 'Sonoo'
WHERE Student_Id = '3'

blocks.text: **c. DELETE:** It is used to remove one or more row from a table.
**Syntax:**

blocks.code: DELETE FROM table_name [WHERE condition];

blocks.text: **For example:**

blocks.code:
DELETE FROM javatpoint
WHERE Author="Sonoo";

blocks.text: Data Control Language
DCL commands are used to grant and take back authority from any database user.
Here are some commands that come under DCL:

items: Grant
Revoke

blocks.text: **a. Grant:** It is used to give user access privileges to a database.
**Example**

blocks.code: GRANT SELECT, UPDATE ON MY_TABLE TO SOME_USER, ANOTHER_USER;

blocks.text: **b. Revoke:** It is used to take back permissions from the user.
**Example**

blocks.code: REVOKE SELECT, UPDATE ON MY_TABLE FROM USER1, USER2;

blocks.text: Transaction Control Language
TCL commands can only use with DML commands like INSERT, DELETE and UPDATE only.
These operations are automatically committed in the database that's why they cannot be used while creating tables or dropping them.
Here are some commands that come under TCL:

items: COMMIT
ROLLBACK
SAVEPOINT

blocks.text: **a. Commit:** Commit command is used to save all the transactions to the database.
**Syntax:**

blocks.code: COMMIT;

**b. Rollback:** Rollback command is used to undo transactions that have not already been saved to the database.
**Syntax:**

blocks.code: ROLLBACK;

blocks.text: **Example:**
**c. SAVEPOINT:** It is used to roll the transaction back to a certain point without rolling back the entire transaction.
**Syntax:**

blocks.code: SAVEPOINT SAVEPOINT_NAME;

DQL is used to fetch the data from the database.
It uses only one command:

blocks.text: DROP TABLE
The SQL **DROP TABLE** statement is used to remove a table definition and all the data, indexes, triggers, constraints and permission specifications for that table.
**NOTE** − You should be very careful while using this command because once a table is deleted then all the information available in that table will also be lost forever.
Syntax
The basic syntax of this DROP TABLE statement is as follows −

blocks.code: DROP TABLE table_name;

blocks.text: INSERT INTO
The SQL **INSERT INTO** Statement is used to add new rows of data to a table in the database.
Syntax
There are two basic syntaxes of the INSERT INTO statement which are shown below.

blocks.code:
INSERT INTO TABLE_NAME (column1, column2, column3,...columnN)
VALUES (value1, value2, value3,...valueN);

blocks.text: Here, column1, column2, column3,...columnN are the names of the columns in the table into which you want to insert the data.

You may not need to specify the column(s) name in the SQL query if you are adding values for all the columns of the table. But make sure the order of the values is in the same order as the columns in the table.
The **SQL INSERT INTO** syntax will be as follows −

The WHERE clause is not only used in the SELECT statement, but it is also used in the UPDATE, DELETE statement, etc., which we would examine in the subsequent chapters.

The SQL **LIKE** clause is used to compare a value to similar values using wildcard operators. There are two wildcards used in conjunction with the LIKE operator.

blocks.text: **1. INNER JOIN**

items: The most important and frequently used of the joins is the **INNER JOIN.** They are also referred to as an **EQUIJOIN.**

The INNER JOIN creates a new result table by combining column values of two tables (table1 and table2) based upon the join-predicate. modules.title: SQL Notes: Constraints, NULL, ALTER & TRUNCATE
modules.summary: Constraints are the rules enforced on the data columns of a table.

blocks.text: Constraints are the rules enforced on the data columns of a table. These are used to limit the type of data that can go into a table. This ensures the accuracy and reliability of the data in the database.
Constraints could be either on a column level or a table level. The column level constraints are applied only to one column, whereas the table level constraints are applied to the whole table.
Following are some of the most commonly used constraints available in SQL. These constraints have already been discussed in SQL - RDBMS Concepts chapter, but it’s worth to revise them at this point.

items: NOT NULL Constraint − Ensures that a column cannot have NULL value.
DEFAULT Constraint − Provides a default value for a column when none is specified.
UNIQUE Constraint − Ensures that all values in a column are different.
PRIMARY Key − Uniquely identifies each row/record in a database table.
FOREIGN Key − Uniquely identifies a row/record in any of the given database table.
CHECK Constraint − The CHECK constraint ensures that all the values in a column satisfies certain conditions.
INDEX − Used to create and retrieve data from the database very quickly.

blocks.text: Constraints can be specified when a table is created with the CREATE TABLE statement or you can use the ALTER TABLE statement to create constraints even after the table is created.

1. **NOT NULL :** By default, a column can hold NULL values. If you do not want a column to have a NULL value, then you need to define such a constraint on this column specifying that NULL is now not allowed for that column.
A NULL is not the same as no data, rather, it represents unknown data.
Example
For example, the following SQL query creates a new table called CUSTOMERS and adds five columns, three of which, are ID NAME and AGE, In this we specify not to accept NULLs −

blocks.code:
CREATE TABLE CUSTOMERS(
  ID INT NOT NULL,
  NAME VARCHAR (20) NOT NULL,
  AGE INT NOT NULL,
  ADDRESS CHAR (25) ,
  SALARY DECIMAL (18, 2),
  PRIMARY KEY (ID)
);

blocks.text: If CUSTOMERS table has already been created, then to add a NOT NULL constraint to the SALARY column in Oracle and MySQL, you would write a query like the one that is shown in the following code block.

blocks.code:
ALTER TABLE CUSTOMERS
  MODIFY SALARY DECIMAL (18, 2) NOT NULL;

blocks.text: 2. **DEFAULT CONSTRAINT:** The DEFAULT constraint provides a default value to a column when the INSERT INTO statement does not provide a specific value.
Example

For example, the following SQL creates a new table called CUSTOMERS and adds five columns. Here, the SALARY column is set to 5000.00 by default, so in case the INSERT INTO statement does not provide a value for this column, then by default this column would be set to 5000.00.

blocks.code:
CREATE TABLE CUSTOMERS(
  ID INT NOT NULL,
  NAME VARCHAR (20) NOT NULL,
  AGE INT NOT NULL,
  ADDRESS CHAR (25) ,
  SALARY DECIMAL (18, 2) DEFAULT 5000.00,
  PRIMARY KEY (ID)
);

blocks.text: If the CUSTOMERS table has already been created, then to add a DEFAULT constraint to the SALARY column, you would write a query like the one which is shown in the code block below.
To drop a DEFAULT constraint, use the following SQL query.

blocks.code:
ALTER TABLE CUSTOMERS
  ALTER COLUMN SALARY DROP DEFAULT;

blocks.text: 3. **UNIQUE CONSTRAINT:** The UNIQUE Constraint prevents two records from having identical values in a column. In the CUSTOMERS table, for example, you might want to prevent two or more people from having an identical age.
Example
For example, the following SQL query creates a new table called CUSTOMERS and adds five columns. Here, the AGE column is set to UNIQUE, so that you cannot have two records with the same age.

blocks.code:
CREATE TABLE CUSTOMERS(
  ID INT NOT NULL,
  NAME VARCHAR (20) NOT NULL,
  AGE INT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  ADDRESS CHAR (25) ,
  SALARY DECIMAL (18, 2),
  PRIMARY KEY (ID)
);

blocks.text: If the CUSTOMERS table has already been created, then to add a UNIQUE constraint to the AGE column. You would write a statement like the query that is given in the code block below.

blocks.code:
ALTER TABLE CUSTOMERS
  MODIFY AGE INT NOT NULL UNIQUE;

blocks.text: You can also use the following syntax, which supports naming the constraint in multiple columns as well.
To drop a UNIQUE constraint, use the following SQL query.

blocks.code:
ALTER TABLE CUSTOMERS
  DROP CONSTRAINT myUniqueConstraint;

blocks.text: If you are using MySQL, then you can use the following syntax −

blocks.code:
ALTER TABLE CUSTOMERS
  DROP INDEX myUniqueConstraint;

blocks.text: 4. **PRIMARY KEY:** A primary key is a field in a table which uniquely identifies each row/record in a database table. Primary keys must contain unique values. A primary key column cannot have NULL values.
A table can have only one primary key, which may consist of single or multiple fields. When multiple fields are used as a primary key, they are called a composite key.
If a table has a primary key defined on any field(s), then you cannot have two records having the same value of that field(s).
**Note** − You would use these concepts while creating database tables.

blocks.code: Create Primary Key

blocks.text: Here is the syntax to define the ID attribute as a primary key in a CUSTOMERS table.

blocks.code:
CREATE TABLE CUSTOMERS(
  ID INT NOT NULL,
  NAME VARCHAR (20) NOT NULL,
  AGE INT NOT NULL,
  ADDRESS CHAR (25) ,
  SALARY DECIMAL (18, 2),
  PRIMARY KEY (ID)
);

blocks.text: To create a PRIMARY KEY constraint on the "ID" column when the CUSTOMERS table already exists, use the following SQL syntax −

blocks.code: ALTER TABLE CUSTOMER ADD PRIMARY KEY (ID);

blocks.text: **NOTE** − If you use the ALTER TABLE statement to add a primary key, the primary key column(s) should have already been declared to not contain NULL values (when the table was first created).
For defining a PRIMARY KEY constraint on multiple columns, use the SQL syntax given below.

blocks.code:
CREATE TABLE CUSTOMERS(
  ID INT NOT NULL,
  NAME VARCHAR (20) NOT NULL,
  AGE INT NOT NULL,
  ADDRESS CHAR (25) ,
  SALARY DECIMAL (18, 2),
  PRIMARY KEY (ID, NAME)
);

blocks.text: To create a PRIMARY KEY constraint on the "ID" and "NAMES" columns when CUSTOMERS table already exists, use thefollowing SQL syntax.
You can clear the primary key constraints from the table with the syntax given below.

blocks.code: ALTER TABLE CUSTOMERS DROP PRIMARY KEY ;

blocks.text: **5.FOREIGN KEY:** A foreign key is a key used to link two tables together. This is sometimes also called as a referencing key.
A Foreign Key is a column or a combination of columns whose values match a Primary Key in a different table.
**The relationship between 2 tables matches the Primary Key in one of the tables with a Foreign Key in the second table.**
If a table has a primary key defined on any field(s), then you cannot have two records having the same value of that field(s).
Example
Consider the structure of the following two tables.
**CUSTOMERS table**

blocks.code:
CREATE TABLE CUSTOMERS(
  ID INT NOT NULL,
  NAME VARCHAR (20) NOT NULL,
  AGE INT NOT NULL,
  ADDRESS CHAR (25) ,
  SALARY DECIMAL (18, 2),
  PRIMARY KEY (ID)
);

blocks.text: **ORDERS table**

blocks.code:
CREATE TABLE ORDERS (
  ID INT NOT NULL,
  DATE DATETIME,
  CUSTOMER_ID INT references CUSTOMERS(ID),
  AMOUNT double,
  PRIMARY KEY (ID)
);

blocks.text: If the ORDERS table has already been created and the foreign key has not yet been set, theuse the syntax for specifying a foreign key by altering a table.
To drop a FOREIGN KEY constraint, use the following SQL syntax.

blocks.code:
ALTER TABLE ORDERS
  DROP FOREIGN KEY;

blocks.text: 6.CHECK CONSTRAINT: The CHECK Constraint enables a condition to check the value being entered into arecord. Ifthe condition evaluates to false, the record violates the constraint and isn't entered the table.
Example
For example, the following program creates a new table called CUSTOMERS and adds five columns. Here, we add a CHECK with AGE column, so that you cannot have any CUSTOMER who is below 18 years.

blocks.code:
CREATE TABLE CUSTOMERS(
  ID INT NOT NULL,
  NAME VARCHAR (20) NOT NULL,
  AGE INT NOT NULL CHECK (AGE >= 18),
  ADDRESS CHAR (25) ,
  SALARY DECIMAL (18, 2),
  PRIMARY KEY (ID)
);

blocks.text: If the CUSTOMERS table has already been created, then to add a CHECK constraint to AGE column, you would write a statement like the one given below.

blocks.code:
ALTER TABLE CUSTOMERS
  MODIFY AGE INT NOT NULL CHECK (AGE >= 18 );

blocks.text: You can also use the following syntax, which supports naming the constraint in multiple columns as well −
To drop a CHECK constraint, use the following SQL syntax. This syntax does not work with MySQL.

blocks.code:
ALTER TABLE CUSTOMERS
  DROP CONSTRAINT myCheckConstraint;
Dropping Constraints

blocks.text: Any constraint that you have defined can be dropped using the ALTER TABLE command with the DROP CONSTRAINT option.
For example, to drop the primary key constraint in the EMPLOYEES table, you can use the following command.

blocks.code: ALTER TABLE EMPLOYEES DROP CONSTRAINT EMPLOYEES_PK;

blocks.text: Some implementations may provide shortcuts for dropping certain constraints. For example, to drop the primary key constraint for a table in Oracle, you can use the following command.

blocks.code: ALTER TABLE EMPLOYEES DROP PRIMARY KEY;

blocks.text: Some implementations allow you to disable constraints. Instead of permanently dropping a constraint from the database, you may want to temporarily disable the constraint and then enable it later.

blocks.code: Integrity Constraints

blocks.text: Integrity constraints are used to ensure accuracy and consistency of the data in a relational database. Data integrity is handled in a relational database through the concept of referential integrity.

There aremany types of integrity constraints that play a role in **Referential Integrity (RI).** These constraints include Primary Key, Foreign Key, Unique Constraints and other constraints which are mentioned above.
NULL Values
The SQL **NULL** is the term used to represent a missing value. A NULL value in a table is a value in a field that appears to be blank.
A field with a NULL value is a field with no value. It is very important to understand that a NULL value is different than a zero value or a field that contains spaces.
Syntax
The basic syntax of **NULL** while creating a table.

blocks.code:
SQL> CREATE TABLE CUSTOMERS(
  ID INT NOT NULL,
  NAME VARCHAR (20) NOT NULL,
  AGE INT NOT NULL,
  ADDRESS CHAR (25) ,
  SALARY DECIMAL (18, 2),
  PRIMARY KEY (ID)
);

blocks.text: Here, **NOT NULL** signifies that column should always accept an explicit value of the given data type. There are two columns where we did not use NOT NULL, which means these columns could be NULL.
A field with a NULL value is the one that has been left blank during the record creation.

ALTER TABLE Command
The SQL **ALTER TABLE** command is used to add, delete or modify columns in an existing table. You should also use the ALTER TABLE command to add and drop various constraints on an existing table.
Syntax
The basic syntax of an ALTER TABLE command to add a **New Column** in an existing table is as follows.

blocks.code: ALTER TABLE table_name ADD column_name datatype;

blocks.text: The basic syntax of an ALTER TABLE command to **DROP COLUMN** in an existing table is as follows.

blocks.code: ALTER TABLE table_name DROP COLUMN column_name;

blocks.text: The basic syntax of an ALTER TABLE command to change the **DATA TYPE** of a column in a table is as follows.

blocks.code: ALTER TABLE table_name MODIFY COLUMN column_name datatype;

blocks.text: A view is nothing more than a SQL statement that is stored in the database with an associated name. A view is actually a composition of a table in the form of a predefined SQL query.
A view can contain all rows of a table or select rows from a table. A view can be created from one or many tables which depends on the written SQL query to create a view.
Views, which are a type of virtual tables allow users to do the following −

items: Structure data in a way that users or classes of users find natural or intuitive.
Restrict access to the data in such a way that a user can see and (sometimes) modify exactly what they need and no more.
Summarize data from various tables which can be used to generate reports.

blocks.text: Creating Views
Database views are created using the **CREATE VIEW** statement. Views can be created from a single table, multiple tables or another view.
To create a view, a user must have the appropriate system privilege according to the specific implementation.
The basic **CREATE VIEW** syntax is as follows −

blocks.code:
CREATE VIEW view_name AS
SELECT column1, column2.....
FROM table_name
WHERE [condition];

blocks.text: You can include multiple tables in your SELECT statement in a similar way as you use them in a normal SQL SELECT query.

The WITH CHECK OPTION

blocks.text: The WITH CHECK OPTION is a CREATE VIEW statement option. The purpose of the WITH CHECK OPTION is to ensure that all UPDATE and INSERTs satisfy the condition(s) in the view definition.
If they do not satisfy the condition(s), the UPDATE or INSERT returns an error.
The following code block has an example of creating same view CUSTOMERS_VIEW with the WITH CHECK OPTION.

blocks.code:
CREATE VIEW CUSTOMERS_VIEW AS
SELECT name, age
FROM CUSTOMERS
WHERE age IS NOT NULL
WITH CHECK OPTION;

blocks.text: The WITH CHECK OPTION in this case should deny the entry of any NULL values in the view's AGE column, because the view is defined by data that does not have a NULL value in the AGE column.
Updating a View
A view can be updated under certain conditions which are given below −

items: The SELECT clause may not contain the keyword DISTINCT.
The SELECT clause may not contain summary functions.
The SELECT clause may not contain set functions.
The SELECT clause may not contain set operators.
The SELECT clause may not contain an ORDER BY clause.
The FROM clause may not contain multiple tables.
The WHERE clause may not contain subqueries.
The query may not contain GROUP BY or HAVING.
Calculated columns may not be updated.
All NOT NULL columns from the base table must be included in the view in order for the INSERT query to function.

Union and Union ALL
UNION

The UNION command is used to select related information from two tables, which is like a JOIN command. However, when using UNION command, all the selected columns need to be of the same data type. With UNION, only distinct values are selected.
**UNION ALL**
UNION ALL command is equal to UNION command, except that UNION ALL selects all the values.

The difference between Union and Union all is that Union all will not eliminate duplicate rows, instead it just pulls all the rows from all the tables fitting your query specifics and combines them into a table.
*A UNION statement effectively does a SELECT DISTINCT on the results set. If you know that all the records returned are unique from your union, use UNION ALL instead, it gives faster results.*

modules.title: Database Non-Relasional (NoSQL)
modules.summary: NoSQL adalah istilah payung untuk database yang tidak menggunakan model tabel relasional.

blocks.text: NoSQL adalah istilah payung untuk database yang tidak menggunakan model tabel relasional. NoSQL muncul untuk menangani data berskala besar (Big Data), data tidak terstruktur, dan kebutuhan skalabilitas horizontal.
Empat Tipe Utama NoSQL
a. Document Store
Menyimpan data sebagai dokumen (umumnya JSON/BSON). Setiap dokumen bisa memiliki struktur berbeda.

items: **Contoh:** MongoDB, CouchDB, Amazon DocumentDB, Firestore.
**Cocok untuk:** CMS, katalog produk, profil pengguna, real-time analytics.

blocks.text: b. Key-Value Store
Model paling sederhana: data disimpan sebagai pasangan kunci dan nilai. Sangat cepat karena akses O(1).

items: **Contoh:** Redis, Memcached, Amazon DynamoDB, Riak.
**Cocok untuk:** caching, session storage, leaderboard, rate limiting.

blocks.code:
# Redis
SET user:1001:nama "Daniel"
GET user:1001:nama
EXPIRE user:1001:nama 3600   # TTL 1 jam
INCR halaman:home:visits
ZADD leaderboard 250 "daniel"

blocks.text: c. Column-Family / Wide-Column Store
Menyimpan data dalam tabel yang sangat lebar dengan kolom dinamis. Dirancang untuk volume data sangat besar dan throughput tinggi.

items: **Contoh:** Apache Cassandra, HBase, ScyllaDB, Google Bigtable.
**Cocok untuk:** time-series, IoT, log, sistem pesan skala besar.

blocks.text: d. Graph Database
Menggunakan node, edge, dan property untuk merepresentasikan dan menyimpan data. Sangat efisien untuk traversal hubungan kompleks.

items: **Contoh:** Neo4j, Amazon Neptune, ArangoDB, JanusGraph.
**Cocok untuk:** jejaring sosial, rekomendasi, deteksi fraud, knowledge graph.

blocks.text: Teorema CAP dan BASE

Teorema CAP menyatakan bahwa sistem terdistribusi hanya bisa memenuhi maksimal dua dari tiga properti: Consistency, Availability, dan Partition Tolerance. Banyak NoSQL memilih AP atau CP, sementara RDBMS umumnya CA dalam mode tunggal.
BASE adalah filosofi alternatif ACID untuk sistem terdistribusi: Basically Available, Soft state, Eventually consistent.

blocks.text: Kapan Memilih SQL?

items: Data sangat terstruktur dan jarang berubah skemanya.
Butuh integritas tinggi (mis. transaksi keuangan, inventory).
Banyak relasi yang membutuhkan JOIN.
Tim sudah familiar dengan SQL.

blocks.text: Kapan Memilih NoSQL?

items: Data tidak terstruktur atau semi-terstruktur (JSON, log, sensor).
Beban tulis sangat tinggi dan butuh distribusi global.
Skema sering berubah (mis. produk e-commerce dengan atribut beragam).
Use case spesifik: caching, graph, time-series.

blocks.text: Polyglot Persistence

Dalam praktiknya, aplikasi modern sering menggunakan kombinasi beberapa database. Misalnya PostgreSQL untuk data transaksi, Redis untuk caching, Elasticsearch untuk full-text search, dan Neo4j untuk fitur rekomendasi. Pendekatan ini disebut polyglot persistence.

Database Relasional (SQL)
2.1 Konsep Dasar Relational Database

Database relasional menyimpan data dalam bentuk tabel yang terdiri atas baris (record) dan kolom (field). Setiap tabel memiliki skema (schema) yang mendefinisikan tipe data setiap kolom. Hubungan (relation) antar tabel dibentuk melalui Primary Key dan Foreign Key.
Istilah Penting

items: **Table:** kumpulan data terstruktur dengan skema tetap.
**Row / Record:** satu baris data dalam tabel.
**Column / Field:** satu kolom yang menyimpan tipe data tertentu.
**Primary Key (PK):** kolom unik untuk mengidentifikasi setiap baris.
**Foreign Key (FK):** kolom yang merujuk Primary Key tabel lain untuk membentuk relasi.
**Index:** struktur tambahan untuk mempercepat pencarian.
**View:** query yang disimpan dan dapat digunakan seperti tabel.

blocks.text: 2.2 Properti ACID
ACID adalah empat properti yang menjamin keandalan transaksi database relasional:

items: **Atomicity:** transaksi berjalan utuh atau tidak sama sekali.
**Consistency:** data tetap valid sebelum dan sesudah transaksi.
**Isolation:** transaksi paralel tidak saling mengganggu.
**Durability:** data yang sudah commit tetap aman meski sistem gagal.

blocks.text: 2.3 Normalisasi Database
Normalisasi adalah proses menyusun tabel agar bebas dari redundansi data dan anomali. Bentuk normal yang umum dipakai:

items: **1NF:** Setiap kolom berisi nilai atomik (tidak berulang).
**2NF:** Memenuhi 1NF, dan tidak ada ketergantungan parsial pada PK komposit.
**3NF:** Memenuhi 2NF, dan tidak ada ketergantungan transitif antar kolom non-key.
**BCNF:** Bentuk lebih ketat dari 3NF.

blocks.text: Bahasa SQL dan Kategorinya
SQL (Structured Query Language) adalah bahasa standar untuk berinteraksi dengan database relasional. Perintah SQL dibagi ke dalam beberapa kategori:
3.1 DDL — Data Definition Language
Digunakan untuk mendefinisikan dan mengubah struktur database (skema).

items: CREATE — membuat database, tabel, view, index, dll.
ALTER — mengubah struktur objek yang sudah ada.
DROP — menghapus objek dari database.
TRUNCATE — mengosongkan isi tabel tanpa menghapus tabelnya.
RENAME — mengganti nama objek.

blocks.text: Contoh DDL
3.2 DML — Data Manipulation Language
Digunakan untuk memanipulasi data di dalam tabel.

items: INSERT — menambahkan baris baru.
UPDATE — mengubah baris yang sudah ada.
DELETE — menghapus baris.
MERGE / UPSERT — gabungan insert + update.

blocks.text: Contoh DML
3.3 DQL — Data Query Language
Khusus untuk membaca / mengambil data. Perintah utamanya adalah SELECT.

blocks.code:
-- Query sederhana
SELECT nama, email FROM pengguna WHERE id = 1;

-- JOIN antar tabel
SELECT p.nama, o.total
FROM pengguna p
INNER JOIN pesanan o ON o.user_id = p.id
WHERE o.total > 100000
ORDER BY o.total DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- Agregasi
SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS jumlah, SUM(total) AS belanja
FROM pesanan
GROUP BY user_id
HAVING SUM(total) > 1000000;

blocks.text: 3.4 DCL — Data Control Language
Digunakan untuk mengatur hak akses pengguna database.

items: GRANT — memberikan izin akses.
REVOKE — mencabut izin akses.

blocks.code:
GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON toko.pengguna TO 'staff'@'%';
REVOKE INSERT ON toko.pengguna FROM 'staff'@'%';

blocks.text: 3.5 TCL — Transaction Control Language
Digunakan untuk mengelola transaksi database.

items: BEGIN / START TRANSACTION — memulai transaksi.
COMMIT — menyimpan perubahan secara permanen.
ROLLBACK — membatalkan perubahan.
SAVEPOINT — titik aman dalam transaksi.

blocks.text: JOIN dan Konsep SQL Lanjutan
4.1 Jenis-Jenis JOIN
JOIN digunakan untuk menggabungkan data dari dua atau lebih tabel berdasarkan kolom yang berelasi.

head: Jenis JOIN
Penjelasan
rows: Semua baris dari tabel kiri + yang cocok dari tabel kanan (NULL jika tidak ada).
Semua baris dari tabel kanan + yang cocok dari tabel kiri.
Semua baris dari kedua tabel, NULL untuk yang tidak punya pasangan.
Tabel di-JOIN dengan dirinya sendiri (mis. relasi atasan-bawahan).

blocks.text: 4.2 Subquery dan CTE
Subquery adalah query di dalam query. CTE (Common Table Expression) menggunakan kata kunci WITH untuk membuat query lebih mudah dibaca dan bisa rekursif.

blocks.code:
-- Subquery
SELECT nama FROM pengguna
WHERE id IN (SELECT user_id FROM pesanan WHERE total > 1000000);

-- CTE
WITH pelanggan_top AS (
  SELECT user_id, SUM(total) AS belanja
  FROM pesanan
  GROUP BY user_id
  HAVING SUM(total) > 5000000
)
SELECT p.nama, t.belanja
FROM pelanggan_top t JOIN pengguna p ON p.id = t.user_id;

blocks.text: 4.3 Window Functions
Fungsi yang dieksekusi pada sekelompok baris yang berkaitan dengan baris saat ini, tanpa menggabungkan baris.

blocks.code:
SELECT
  user_id,
  total,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY tanggal DESC) AS urutan,
  SUM(total)  OVER (PARTITION BY user_id) AS total_per_user
FROM pesanan;

blocks.text: 4.4 Index, View, dan Stored Procedure

items: **Index:** mempercepat SELECT, namun memperlambat INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE.
**View:** query yang disimpan dengan nama, dapat dipakai layaknya tabel.
**Stored Procedure:** blok kode SQL yang disimpan di database dan bisa dipanggil berulang.
**Trigger:** kode yang otomatis dijalankan saat ada event tertentu (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE).

blocks.text: Studi Kasus dan Latihan Praktik
8.1 Studi Kasus: Skema Toko Online (SQL)
Berikut contoh skema relasional sederhana untuk e-commerce. Latihlah membuatnya dari nol di MySQL atau PostgreSQL.
8.2 Latihan SQL

items: Tampilkan 10 produk termahal.
Tampilkan 5 pelanggan dengan total belanja terbesar bulan ini.
Cari produk yang stoknya kurang dari 10.
Hitung jumlah pesanan per hari selama 30 hari terakhir.
Buat view pelanggan_aktif untuk pelanggan dengan minimal 3 pesanan.

blocks.text: Penutup

Belajar database adalah perjalanan jangka panjang. Mulailah dari fondasi SQL relasional, kuasai konsep normalisasi, indexing, dan transaksi. Setelah merasa nyaman, lanjutkan ke dunia NoSQL dengan mencoba MongoDB untuk dokumen, Redis untuk caching, dan Neo4j untuk graph. Akhirnya, eksplorasi NewSQL dan database cloud akan memperluas wawasan tentang skala global.
Kunci sukses: konsisten praktik, bangun proyek nyata, dan jangan takut salah. Setiap query yang lambat atau skema yang berantakan adalah pelajaran berharga untuk menjadi engineer yang lebih baik.
**Selamat belajar, Daniel — semoga dokumentasi ini menjadi peta perjalananmu menjelajahi dunia database!**
